title: Evaluation of the Effects of Two Biostimulators on Skin Quality: A Split-Face Study Comparing a Hyaluronic Acid Gel Enriched with Glycine, L-Proline, and Calcium Hydroxylapatite (CaHA) with a Non-Cross-Linked Hyaluronic Acid Gel (HA)
summary: This study investigates how well two different hyaluronic acid preparations improve facial skin quality. 20 women between 18 and 65 years of age take part. Each participant receives both products at the same time, one injected into each half of the face: one side receives a hyaluronic acid gel enriched with glycine, L-proline and calcium hydroxyapatite (NEAUVIA Hydro Deluxe), the other side a conventional, non-cross-linked hyaluronic acid gel (Profhilo®). This allows a direct, within-person comparison of how well each product works. Treatment is given in two sessions about four weeks apart. Over a total of around 10 months, skin hydration, elasticity, thickness and other skin properties are measured, photographs are taken, and both participants and trained experts assess satisfaction and skin improvement. The aim is to determine whether the calcium-hydroxyapatite-containing product is equivalent or superior to conventional hyaluronic acid in improving skin quality.
conditions: loss of skin quality in healthy skin

interventions.name: NEAUVIA Hydro Deluxe (HACaHA) – 2,5 mL, one side of the face
Profhilo® (non-cross-linked HA) – 2 mL, contralateral side of the face

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Female sex
Age between 18 and 65 years (inclusive)
Generally good state of health
Understanding of and agreement to the study procedures
Sufficient time availability for the duration of the study
No inflammatory skin conditions in the treatment area
Self-assessed skin quality score ≤ 50% on the questionnaire
Expert rating of at least "mild" (1) at rest and "moderate" (2) at maximum smiling, at V1
SASSQ rating with at least three of six categories scoring ≥ 2 ("moderate"), at V1
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnancy, breastfeeding, or planned pregnancy / egg donation
Use or topical application of medications affecting skin quality (e.g., retinoids)
Use of anticoagulants or anti-inflammatory drugs
Clinically relevant skin, autoimmune, or collagen diseases
Smoking (current or within the last 6 months)
Previous invasive or minimally invasive aesthetic treatments in the study area within the last 12 months
Permanent fillers and implants in the study area
Excessive UV exposure, current or past
Tattoos or significant scars on the face
Participation in another clinical study within the last 30 days
Contact of the study area with substances, skincare products, or cleaning products, as well as water, within the last 6 hours
